questions.q: If matrix $A$ has size $3 \times 4$ and matrix $B$ has size $4 \times 2$, what is the size of the product $A B$?
questions.answer: An $m \times k$ matrix multiplied by a $k \times n$ matrix produces an $m \times n$ matrix. Here $(3 \times 4) \times (4 \times 2) = 3 \times 2$.

questions.q: Is matrix multiplication commutative in general ($A B = B A$)?
choices: No, $A B \neq B A$ in general even when both products are defined
Yes, multiplication of numbers and matrices is always commutative
Only if the entries are integers
Yes, provided both matrices are square
questions.answer: Matrix multiplication is fundamentally non-commutative: in general, $A B \neq B A$.

questions.q: What is $(A B)^T$ equal to in terms of the transposes $A^T$ and $B^T$?
questions.answer: The transpose of a product reverses order: $(A B)^T = B^T A^T$.

sections.heading: Section 2: Matrix Inverses and Elementary Matrices

questions.q: Find the inverse of the $2 \times 2$ matrix $A = [[4, 7], [1, 2]]$.

choices: A matrix obtained by performing a single elementary row operation on an identity matrix
A matrix with exactly one non-zero row
questions.answer: An elementary matrix $E$ represents a single row operation; multiplying $E A$ performs that row operation on $A$.

questions.q: If $A, B, C$ are invertible square matrices, what is $(A B C)^{-1}$?
questions.answer: Inverting a product reverses the sequence of all factors: $(A B C)^{-1} = C^{-1} B^{-1} A^{-1}$.

sections.heading: Section 3: Symmetric, Orthogonal, and Special Matrices

questions.q: A square matrix $A$ is symmetric if and only if:
questions.answer: A matrix is symmetric when it equals its own transpose: $A^T = A$ ($a_{ij} = a_{ji}$ for all $i, j$).
An orthogonal matrix has orthonormal columns, which means $Q^T Q = I$ and therefore $Q^{-1} = Q^T$.

questions.q: If $Q$ is an orthogonal matrix, what are the possible values for $\det(Q)$?

sections.heading: Section 4: Linear Transformations and Standard Matrices

questions.q: A transformation $T: \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}^m$ is linear if and only if for all vectors $\mathbf{u}, \mathbf{v}$ and scalars $c$:
questions.answer: Linearity is defined by preservation of vector addition and scalar multiplication: $T(c\mathbf{u} + d\mathbf{v}) = cT(\mathbf{u}) + dT(\mathbf{v})$.

questions.q: What is the standard matrix for counterclockwise rotation in $\mathbb{R}^2$ by angle $\theta$?
questions.answer: Rotating $[1, 0]^T$ gives $[\cos\theta, \sin\theta]^T$, and rotating $[0, 1]^T$ gives $[-\sin\theta, \cos\theta]^T$, giving $[[\cos\theta, -\sin\theta], [\sin\theta, \cos\theta]]$.

questions.q: What is the standard matrix for reflection across the $x$-axis in $\mathbb{R}^2$?
questions.answer: Reflecting across the $x$-axis keeps $x$ the same and negates $y$: $T([x, y]^T) = [x, -y]^T$, so the matrix is $[[1, 0], [0, -1]]$.
